literature_notes: All six ledger lines (L1–L6) describe C-terminal GFP fusions on PTTG1IP (the paralog), not PTTG1IP2. Two disqualifying problems compound each other. First, PTTG1IP and PTTG1IP2 are paralogs, not orthologs; the ledger rule permitting indirect evidence specifies 'a close ortholog', which is a species-level relationship, not a paralog relationship. Second, even if the most generous reading were applied and PTTG1IP were treated as an indirect precedent, the C-terminal GFP fusions described in every ledger line land on the INTRACELLULAR face of PTTG1IP2: the topology landmarks place residues 119–154 (including the C-terminus at residue 154) in the cytoplasm. A C-terminal tag therefore cannot serve as an extracellular surface tag. The extracellular domain of PTTG1IP2 (residues 27–97, after signal-peptide cleavage) has no ledger support whatsoever for any tag insertion. Zero qualifying extracellular sites result.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusions on the paralog PTTG1IP (L1–L6) map to the intracellular C-terminus of PTTG1IP2 (residues 119–154 are cytoplasmic per topology landmarks); valid for an intracellular label but not an extracellular surface tag.
